description:
We are high school students from Van, Turkey.

Working on the Astronaut Health Monitoring Software challenge. We will build a web dashboard that shows vital signs, alerts, and recommendations.

Roles: Backend (PHP), Frontend (HTML/CSS/JS + Chart.js), UI/Design, Testing.

Excited for NASA Space Apps 2026!
summary:
On a Mars transit, a message from Earth can take up to 22 minutes one way. Real-time medical help from Mission Control is no longer possible, while the crew faces radiation, bone loss, vision damage (SANS), immune problems and life-support faults.

VanBlue Aegis is an onboard AI flight surgeon: a mission-control web dashboard that watches a simulated four-person crew around the clock. It reads live telemetry (heart rate, SpO2, blood pressure, temperature, radiation dose) and checks it against NASA-STD-3001 limits. It also uses MSL RAD deep-space dosimetry, live NASA DONKI space weather, NASA OSDR biology studies and NASA HRP risk evidence. When a solar particle event hits, Aegis raises the alarm, sends the crew to the storm shelter and logs the event on its own. Astronauts can describe symptoms by voice or text and get structured advice in milliseconds instead of 27 minutes.

It matters because future Artemis and Mars crews will need medical autonomy. The same architecture can bring remote health monitoring to places on Earth far from a doctor, such as rural villages, disaster zones, polar stations and ships at sea.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

VanBlue Aegis is an autonomous "onboard medical officer" for a deep-space crew. On a Mars transit, Earth can be up to 22 light-minutes away, so the crew cannot wait for a doctor's answer. Aegis watches every astronaut continuously, explains risks and acts on its own when Earth cannot respond in time.

HOW IT WORKS

- Live telemetry: simulated vitals for four fictional astronauts (heart rate, SpO2, blood pressure, temperature, respiration, hydration, radiation dose), updated every 2 seconds.

- Autonomous triage: every reading is checked against NASA-STD-3001 limits and clinical reference ranges. Every triage, consultation and medication is stored as a health event.

- Radiation & space weather: cumulative dose vs. the NASA career limit, built on MSL RAD cruise dosimetry (~1.84 mSv/day), plus live solar flares and CMEs from NASA DONKI. A solar particle event triggers a red alert, a storm-shelter countdown and an automatic log entry.

- AI Flight Surgeon: astronauts describe symptoms by voice or text (photos can be attached). The AI sees live vitals and mission context, detects red-flag symptoms and gives structured advice in milliseconds instead of a 27-minute round trip. If the AI service is offline, a rule-based engine answers, so the system never goes silent.

- Health Detective: separates environmental causes (cabin CO2, sensor fault) from individual illness.

- Space conditions: projects bone loss, muscle atrophy, SANS and more by mission day, based on NASA HRP evidence.

- Also included: countermeasure schedule (ARED, CEVIS, LBNP), cognitive PVT tests, ship pharmacy inventory, printable medical reports, a NASA Data Center and a guided jury demo tour.

BENEFITS & IMPACT

In space, it gives Artemis and Mars crews, flight surgeons and mission planners medical support that works without Earth. On Earth, the same architecture can bring remote health monitoring to places far from a doctor: rural villages in Van, earthquake zones, Antarctic stations and ships at sea.

TOOLS & LANGUAGES

PHP 8.5, Laravel 13, SQLite, Blade, Tailwind CSS 4, vanilla JavaScript, Apache ECharts 5.5, Web Speech API (voice), Google Gemini API, PHPUnit, Laravel Pint, Vite.

CREATIVITY

A holographic mission-control interface that calculates light-speed delay live, talks to the crew by voice, and makes autonomous decisions grounded in real NASA data, not just generic AI answers.

PHP 8.5, Laravel 13, SQLite, Blade, Tailwind CSS 4, vanilla JavaScript, Apache ECharts 5.5, Web Speech API (voice), Google Gemini API, PHPUnit, Laravel Pint, Vite.

A holographic mission-control interface that calculates light-speed delay live, talks to the crew by voice, and makes autonomous decisions grounded in real NASA data, not just generic AI answers.

Reliability (every live API has an offline fallback, so the demo never breaks), data transparency (each value is labelled as live NASA data, NASA archive, model or simulation), safety (AI answers are labelled as decision support, not diagnosis) and privacy (the crew is fictional, and no real personal data is used).
